punchline: Twenty-two people in one room chose the hosts of two World Cups, and two others were already suspended.
thirty_sec: On 2 December 2010 FIFA's executive committee picked Russia for 2018 and Qatar for 2022. Two of its 24 members had been suspended after a Sunday Times sting, in which reporters posing as lobbyists recorded them discussing the sale of their votes. Twenty-two voted. Qatar beat the United States 14 to 8 in the last round. A tiny electorate means each voter can be courted one by one.
